rows.description: I decide who is in and who is out, and I love the power. It feels safe but I hurt people. Wise leaders include others and see that ruling by fear leaves friends who do not care for me.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, betrayal, envy, rejection
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: affection, fear, trust, hurt

rows.description: I go along with mean things because I fear being kicked out of the group. Belonging built on fear is fragile. Wise: quietly refuse one thing and see who still stands by me.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, betrayal, envy, rejection
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: fear, nostalgia

rows.description: I stop chasing the popular group and enjoy the two friends who like me. Smaller friendship circles can be deeper. Acceptance is not defeat; it frees energy for real bonds.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, envy, rejection
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17

rows.description: My friend joined the clique and dropped me. I feel betrayed and angry. I let myself feel it, tell someone and avoid revenge. Perhaps she feels torn too. I can leave the door open and protect myself.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, envy, rejection
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: anger

rows.description: I notice my teacher looks tired and worried today. Seeing teachers as people makes me kinder and calmer in class. I can help pick up books or be quiet. Kids who notice feelings grow wise.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, favouritism, fear, gratitude, humiliation
related mind states: anxiety, tiredness, calm, empathy

rows.description: My favourite teacher was unfair to me once, and I am shocked. Adults can make mistakes. I can politely tell her how I felt. Cutting her off forever or mocking her is not needed.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, favouritism, fear, gratitude, humiliation
related mind states: disappointment, surprise

rows.description: The teacher seems to like some kids more, and I feel invisible. It may be real or not. I do my best, ask for help, and speak to her or a parent if unfair. Sulking helps nobody.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, disillusionment, fear, gratitude, humiliation

rows.description: I am scared of my strict teacher and my hands shake. Fear of getting it wrong blocks learning. I can ask a question after class and see her softer side. Many strict teachers care.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, disillusionment, favouritism, gratitude, humiliation
related mind states: fear

rows.description: Teacher stayed late to help me understand fractions and I feel cared for. I say thank you and try harder. Feeling supported grows confidence more than any scolding.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, disillusionment, favouritism, fear, humiliation
related mind states: gratitude

rows.description: The teacher mocked me in front of the class and I wanted to vanish. That was wrong of her. I tell my parents so they can raise it with the school. Adults should correct, not shame.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, disillusionment, favouritism, fear, gratitude
related mind states: shame, humiliation
